title: Planetary gearbox
summary: ratio and size in, gears that mesh
description: A printable single-stage planetary reducer for a NEMA stepper, from the reduction and the size you ask for: true involute teeth with profile shift, a planet count that always assembles, ball bearings on steel pins, six print plates that each fit a 220 mm bed, and a slider that turns every gear by the true kinematics.
process: 3D printing (FDM), steel dowel pins and standard ball bearings

difficulty.rationale: Involute flanks drawn as formula arcs, internal-gear interference limits, ranges coupled across the form, closed-form tooth areas, meshes measured under a drive angle, and six print plates.

standards: KHK Gear Technical Reference, printed edition (Gear Guide 1): Tables 1.1, 3.1, 3.2 (JIS B 1701-2, ISO 54 series I modules), 3.5, 4.6, 6.1, 17.2; eq. 3.4, 3.5, 3.7 to 3.10, 4.4 to 4.9, 10.9, 17.1 to 17.6
NASA TM-82614, Savage, Coy, Townsend, Optimal Tooth Numbers for Compact Standard Spur Gear Sets (1981): eq. 1 to 6, contact ratio and involute interference of internal pairs
NEMA 14, 17, 23 mounting face from the NEMA size table at hallikainen.org; 17HS4401 shaft and torque as listed by Bits & Parts
Bearing sizes (DIN 625-1, 60 and 618 series) from distributor listings; 220 x 220 mm bed of the Creality Ender-3 family from Creality's own Ender series parameter comparison
materials: PETG or ABS, printed (motor plate, ring gear, cover, two carrier plates, sun, planets, output hub, output flange)
Hardened steel dowel pins, one per planet, cut to the length the form gives (ISO 8734 type)
Deep groove ball bearings: one per planet (624, 625, 626 or 608, 60 series) and two 618-series for the output (61804, 61805 or 61807)
M3 screws and M3 heat-set inserts; the motor's own screws
